text: At Bag End, Gandalf threw Bilbo's old ring into the fire. When Frodo picked it out, fine letters of fire showed on the band, and Gandalf named it the One Ring.
After his farewell party, Bilbo vanished from the Shire. He argued with Gandalf before he agreed to leave the ring behind for Frodo.
Frodo, Sam and Pippin set out from Bag End on foot, carrying the Ring east toward Buckland.
A Black Rider, one of the Nazgûl, stopped on the road and sniffed the air while the hobbits hid among the roots of a tree.
At the Prancing Pony, Frodo gave his name as Mr. Underhill. During a song on a table, the Ring slipped onto his finger and he vanished in front of the common room.
A Ranger called Strider offered to guide the hobbits to Rivendell. A late letter from Gandalf told them they could trust him.
Before dawn, the beds in the hobbits' room at the inn were slashed. Their ponies had been driven off in the night.
On Weathertop, five of the Nazgûl came to the camp at night. Frodo put on the Ring and the Witch-king stabbed him with a Morgul-blade.
Strider found a stone on Weathertop marked with the rune G and three strokes, a sign that Gandalf had been there.
At the Ford of Bruinen, the river rose in a flood shaped like white horses and swept the Ringwraiths away.
At the Council of Elrond, Gandalf told how Sauron forged the One Ring in secret after the Elven-smiths of Eregion had made the other Rings of Power.
The Council agreed that the Ring could not be hidden or used, only destroyed in the fire where it was made. Frodo said he would take it.
Before the Company left Rivendell, Bilbo gave Frodo his sword Sting and a coat of mithril.
At the West-gate of Moria, the Watcher in the Water seized Frodo by the ankle before the Company fled inside.
In the Chamber of Mazarbul the Company found Balin's tomb and a torn book of records kept by his dwarves.
On the Bridge of Khazad-dûm, Gandalf stood against the Balrog and fell with it into the dark.
Elves of Lothlórien led the Company blindfolded to Caras Galadhon. Gimli agreed only once everyone else was blindfolded too.
In Lothlórien, Galadriel let Frodo look into her mirror, and he saw the Eye searching for him. She refused the Ring when he offered it to her.
Before the Company left Lothlórien, Galadriel gave Frodo a phial holding the light of Eärendil's star.
On the slopes of Amon Hen, Boromir tried to take the Ring from Frodo, who put it on and ran.
Boromir's horn was ringing in the woods below Amon Hen as orcs fell on Merry and Pippin.
Frodo took a boat to cross the river alone, but Sam waded in after him and nearly drowned.
In the tower of Cirith Ungol, Sam rescued Frodo and gave back the Ring he had been carrying.
The hobbits were caught up in a column of orcs on the road and marched north until they slipped away at a crossroads.
On the slopes of Mount Doom, Sam carried Frodo when he could no longer walk under the weight of the Ring.
In the Sammath Naur, Frodo claimed the Ring for himself. Gollum bit it from his finger and fell with it into the fire.
As the Ring was destroyed, Barad-dûr fell and the Nazgûl burned in the air. The eagles carried the hobbits out of the fire.
Frodo sailed from the Grey Havens with Bilbo, Gandalf, Elrond and Galadriel. Sam watched the ship until it was gone.
